rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali's report says Gabriel had never seen the angel before; Gabriel calls him the closest of creation to God.
rows.anchor: يا جبريل ! من هذا ؟ ) قال : والذي بعثك بالحق ! إني لأقرب الخلق مكانا

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: The angel took Muhammad forward, and Muhammad led the people of heaven, including Adam and Noah, in prayer.
rows.anchor: ثم أخذ الملك بيد محمد صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم فقدمه , فأم بأهل السماء فيهم آدم ونوح

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says that on that day God completed Muhammad's distinction over the inhabitants of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين راويه : فيومئذ أكمل الله لمحمد - صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the Night Journey uniquely honored Muhammad; this sura also contains his station of greatest intercession, established in sound reports and Sunni consensus.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الزبير : وقد حصل منه تفضيله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم - وشرف وكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says no other Qur'anic sura contains as many of Muhammad's special distinctions over all prophets as this one.
rows.anchor: ولا أعلم في الكتاب العزيز سورة تضمنت من خصائصه صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the extraordinary Night Journey demonstrated God's power and Muhammad's signs in a brief time, the passage turns to signs granted to Moses over a very long journey from Egypt to the holy land.
rows.anchor: ولما ثبت بهذه الخارقة ما أخبر به عن نفسه المقدسة من عظيم القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was especially blessed for this community: he directed Muhammad to ask God to reduce the prayers from fifty to five while retaining the reward of fifty.
rows.anchor: موسى عليه السلام الذي كان أعظم الأنبياء بركة على هذه الأمية ليلة الإسراء لما أرشد النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم إليه من مراجعة الله تعالى في تخفيف الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author contrasts Muhammad's one-night journey with Moses' scripture and Israel's journey, which took over forty years; Moses' own communion followed forty days of fasting and retreat.
rows.anchor: وكان إيتاء موسى عليه السلام الكتاب في نيف وأربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author observes that the two Israelite generations differ just as the two Books differ.
rows.anchor: فقد بان الفصل بين الإسرائيلين كما بان الفصل بين الكتابين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the two scouts who kept the covenant survived from those who left Egypt; the others died before reaching the holy land.
rows.anchor: إلا ( النقيبين الموفين ) بالعهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel traveled from Egypt toward Jerusalem for forty years without reaching it; those who left Egypt died except the two who kept the covenant.
rows.anchor: أقاموا سائرين إليها أربعين سنة ولم يصلوا

rows.speaker: كثير من العلماء
rows.claim: Many scholars say Israel wandered in the wilderness for forty years; the Torah instead says they circled Mount Edom during that period.
rows.anchor: قال كثير من العلماء , أو أنهم كانوا في هذه المدة يدورون حول جبل أدوم كما في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between Muhammad's short journey and Israel's long, unsuccessful journey shows that God acts according to his choice and wisdom.
rows.anchor: فثبت أنا إنما نفعل بالاختيار على حسب ما نراه من الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book served as guidance for Israel in just conduct, monotheism, and legal rulings.
rows.anchor: بالحمل على العدل في التوحيد والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by mentioning Muhammad's Night Journey first and Moses' Book second, implying the corresponding omitted acts for each prophet; this is ihtibāk.
rows.anchor: فذكر الإسراء أولا دليل على حذف مثله لموسى عليه السلام ثانيا , وذكر إيتاء الكتاب ثانيا دليل على حذف مثله أولا , فالآية من الاحتباك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads the verb in «ألا تتخذوا» with yāʾ, while the other readers use tāʾ.
rows.anchor: بالياء التحتية في قراءة أبي عمرون وبالفوقانية في قراءة الباقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «ذُرِّيَّةَ» is accusative as specification in Abu ʿAmr's reading and a vocative in the others.
rows.anchor: على الاختصاص في قراءة أبي عمرو , وعلى النداء عند الباقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form افتعال suggests that turning from God requires a struggle against the abundant proofs of his oneness, his favors, and the soul's natural inclination toward him.
rows.anchor: فنبه بصيغة الافتعال على أنه - لكثرة ما على وحدانيته من الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A «وكيل» is a Lord to whom people entrust their affairs; relying on idols or intermediaries for access or intercession is foolish because they cannot provide what God provides.
rows.anchor: أي ربا يكلون أمورهم إليه ويعتمدون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the preposition «من دوني» points to all ranks beneath God's incomparable majesty; a «وكيل» is the one entrusted with affairs.
rows.anchor: من دوني } وقال تعالى : { وكيلا * } أي ربا يكلون أمورهم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author parses «إنه كان» as an innate condition and «عبدا شكورا» as exceptionally grateful.
rows.anchor: { إنه كان } أي كونا جبليا { عبدا شكروا * } أي مبالغا في الشكر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Muhammad declared himself the master of humankind on Judgment Day while eating a shoulder of meat that he liked.
rows.anchor: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم بلحم فرفع إليه الذراع وكانت تعجبه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: At the end of the intercession report, Muhammad is told to admit those of his community without reckoning through the right gate of Paradise; they share the other gates with everyone else.
rows.anchor: أدخل من أمتك من لا حساب عليهم من الباب الأيمن من أبواب الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah thanked God by directing every blessing to its intended purpose; his descendants should imitate him and Abraham in gratitude rather than imitate disbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي مبالغا في الشكر الذي هو صرف جميع ما أنعم الله به فيما خلقه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewarded Noah's gratitude by placing prophethood and scripture among his descendants, as he did for Abraham, and the author urges Noah's descendants to emulate both forefathers.
rows.anchor: فأحسن إليه لشكره بأن جعل في ذريته النبوة والكتاب كما فعل بإبراهيم عليه السلام لأنه كان شاكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is singled out because no one was granted as much delay and respite as his people before God destroyed them all.
rows.anchor: وخص نوحا عليه السلام لأنه ما أملى لأحد ما أملى لقومه ولا أمهل أحدا ما أمهلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flood's destruction and gradual recession show that God is not hasty: he may accomplish great works quickly and lesser works over long periods, always according to wisdom.
rows.anchor: فثبت أنه منزه عن العجلة , وأنه سبحانه تارة يفعل الأمور الكثيرة الشاقة في أسرع وقت

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari's report from Abu Hurayra recounts the great intercession: when humanity reaches Noah, they plead that God called him a grateful servant, but he redirects them until they reach Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وأنهم يقولون لنوح عليه السلام : وقد سماك الله عبدا شكورا , وكلهم يتبرأ ويحيل على من بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author next invokes Moses' Book as proof that its attribution to God is true and that God's knowledge and power encompass history; delayed punishment should not be mistaken for acquiescence.
rows.anchor: ثم أتبع ذلك ما يدل على شرف كتاب موسى وصحة نسبته إليه تعالى بما يقتضي شمول العلم وتمام القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God decisively disclosed by revelation to Israel, through the Book conveyed by Moses, that they would commit corruption twice and become greatly arrogant in the holy land.
rows.anchor: وقضينا } أي بعظمتنا بالوحي المقطوع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «قضينا» means settling and deciding a matter firmly; the predicted arrogance follows a long reprieve and forgetfulness of God's wisdom.
rows.anchor: والقضاء : فصل الأمر على إحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «الأرض» is the sacred land, treated as the land itself because of its special honor; Israel would corrupt it twice and arrogantly overreach.
rows.anchor: في الأرض } أي المقدسة التي كأنها لشرفها هي الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the first punishment's appointed time came, God sent servants against Israel, emphasizing their enmity and his power; they possessed a severe capacity for punishment and warfare.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاء وعد أولاهما } أي وقته الذي حددناه له للانتقام فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «فجاسوا خلال الديار» means the attackers searched repeatedly through the homes with oppression and harsh force; «جاس» is seeking something exhaustively.
rows.anchor: شديد فجاسوا } أي ترددوا مع الظلم والعسف وشديد السطوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «خلال» means the spaces between things, often involving weakness.
rows.anchor: والخلال : انفراج ما بين الشيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is an accomplished promise that cannot fail, since nothing can obstruct God or alter his word.
rows.anchor: أي لا شك في وقوعه ولا بد أن يفعل لأنه لا حائل بيننا وبينه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the first attackers as Goliath and his troops.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنهم جالوت وجنوده

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib identifies the first attackers as Nebuchadnezzar and his troops.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب أنهم بختنصر وجنوده

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the first attackers as the Amalekites.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : العمالقة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies the first attackers as Sennacherib and his troops.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير : سنجاريب وجنوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites curses in the Torah's fifth book as a possible prediction of the first punishment: disobedience would bring disease, losses, invasion, siege, and starvation.
rows.anchor: قال في السفر الخامس من التوراة إشارة إلى هذه المرة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After humiliation, God restored Israel's victory and favor, supplying wealth, sons, and more people ready to mobilize than their enemy.
rows.anchor: ثم رددنا لكم الكرة عليهم وأمددناكم بأموال وبنين وجعلناكم أكثر نفيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delayed restoration displays God's power to reverse a long period of subjection once the people have been cleansed and disciplined.
rows.anchor: بين أنه مقتدر على إدالته على من قهره بعد طول ذله إذا نقاه من درنه وهذبه من ذنوبه

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators place Israel's restored ascendancy in David's time.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين : في زمان داود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects identifying this restoration with David's time because Solomon, not David, completed the mosque; the later invasion is said to enter it as on the first occasion.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه ليس المراد بها المرة ما كان على يدي داود عليه السلام لأن الله يقول في هذه المرة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the Philistines and others had subdued Israel before David and that David delivered them; the author points to the Psalms as evidence of their earlier defeat and later restoration.
rows.anchor: والذي عز من قال أن بني إسرائيل كانوا قهروا قبل داود عليه السلام من الفلسطينين وغيرهم , ثم كان خلاصهم على يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Psalm 13's hope that God will restore his people's captivity and Psalm 44's lament that Israel has suffered defeat despite not abandoning God's name or covenant.
rows.anchor: من يعطي صهيون الخلاص لإسرائيل ؟ إذا رد الرب سبي شعبه يتهلل يعقوب ويفرح إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited psalm portrays foreign nations invading God's inheritance, defiling the sanctuary, destroying Jerusalem, and killing his servants; Israel asks God for help, forgiveness, and vindication.
rows.anchor: اللهم ! إن الأمم دخلت ميراثك ونجست هيكل قدسك , جعلوا أورشليم خرابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another psalm asks the Shepherd of Israel to restore the people, recalling the vine that God brought from Egypt and planted, later broken down and ravaged by animals.
rows.anchor: أنت نقلت الكرمة من مصر , طردت الشعوب وغرستها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 84 says God was once pleased with the land, restored Jacob's captivity, forgave his people's sins, and withdrew his anger.
rows.anchor: رضيت يا رب عن أرضك , ورددت سبي يعقوب , غفرت ذنوب شعبك سترت جميع خطاياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 88 recalls God's covenant with David and his promised elevation, then laments that the anointed king was rejected, his defenses ruined, and his reign diminished.
rows.anchor: إني جعلت عونا للقوى , رفعت مختارا من شعبي , ووجدت داود عبدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited prayer asks God to rescue Israel from the nations and gather the people so they may praise him.
rows.anchor: خلصنا يا إلهنا واجمعنا من الأمم لنشكر اسمك القدوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 125 celebrates the return of Zion's captives and compares it to joyful harvest after sowing in tears.
rows.anchor: إذا رد الرب سبي صهيون صرنا كالمغتربين , حينئذ تمتلئ أفواهنا فرحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Psalm 136 recalls the Babylonian exile and vengeance sought against Edom; the author reads it as foretelling what Nebuchadnezzar would do.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي في هذا المزمور إيذان بما يحل بهم من بختنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if old-scripture wording that implies a deficiency, such as calling God «Father», were authentic, Islamic law does not permit its use.
rows.anchor: ما كان فيما ينقل من هذه الكتب القديمة من لفظة توهم نقصا كالأب ونحوه فإنها على تقدير صحتها عنهم لا يجوز إطلاقها في شرعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies the Qur'anic restoration as the return under Cyrus in Ezra's era and identifies Nebuchadnezzar's forces as the first conquerors.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الأدلة المذكورة في القرآن في هذه الكرة هي التي كانت في أيام عزير عليه السلام على يد كورش ملك الفرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jeremiah's prophecies, begun under Josiah and continued through Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, warned that Babylon would capture Jerusalem and exile Zedekiah, then return the people after seventy years.
rows.anchor: ويستمرون في أسرهم سبعين سنة ثم يردهم الله تعالى إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: إرميا
rows.claim: Jeremiah recounts that God called him before birth as a prophet to nations; God tells him not to fear because he will rescue him and put his words in his mouth.
rows.anchor: قال إرميا عليه السلام : إن الله تعالى قال لي : من قبل أن أصورك في البطن عرفتك

rows.speaker: إرميا
rows.claim: Jeremiah's vision of an almond branch signifies that God is hastening to fulfill his word; the northward pot signifies disaster coming against Judah from the north.
rows.anchor: رأيت عصنا من شجر اللوز

rows.speaker: إرميا
rows.claim: Jeremiah is told that invading forces will encircle Jerusalem and Judah's towns, because the people forsook God, burned incense to foreign gods, and worshiped handmade idols.
rows.anchor: وأنتقم منهم بأحكام وقضائي من أجل جميع سرورهم وبسوء أعمالهم , لأنهم اجتنبوني وبخروا لآلهة غريبة

rows.speaker: إرميا
rows.claim: God commissions Jeremiah to warn Judah's rulers and people, promising that they cannot overpower him because God made him like an iron pillar and bronze wall.
rows.anchor: وقد جعلتك اليوم كالقرية العزيزة الممتنعة , ومثل قضيب من حديد , وصيرتك مثل سور من نحاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Jeremiah delivered eloquent, moving warnings for about four booklets, while false prophets reassured the people and provoked the authorities against him.
rows.anchor: وكان المتنبئون الكذبة يقومون فيهم بخلاف ذلك مما يؤمنهم إلى أن ضربوا إرميا ليترك عنهم مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: إرميا
rows.claim: Jeremiah tells the false prophet Hananiah that God did not send him and that he will die that year for leading the people into falsehood; Hananiah dies in the seventh month.
rows.anchor: ومن أجل هذا يقول الرب : هو ذا أطرحك عن وجه الأرض , وفي هذه السنة تموت

rows.speaker: إرميا
rows.claim: While imprisoned, Jeremiah dictates God's warning to Baruch, who reads it to the people during a fast in hope that they will repent and avert the threatened disaster.
rows.anchor: فدعا باروخ بن ناريا الكاتب وأمره بكتابة ما أنطقه به الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: King Jehoiakim tore up and burned Jeremiah's scroll; God ordered a replacement with an added prophecy that Jehoiakim would have no successor on David's throne and would receive a dishonorable burial.
rows.anchor: فشققها وأحرقها بالنار , فأمره الله أن يكتب صحيفة أخرى مثلها ويزيد ما يأمره الله به

rows.speaker: إرميا
rows.claim: Jeremiah tells Zedekiah that Babylon will seize Jerusalem, take the king to Babylon, and that the king will die peacefully rather than in battle.
rows.anchor: هوذا أدفع هذه القرية وصديقيا ملك يهوذا في يدي ملك بابل ويضبطها

rows.speaker: إرميا
rows.claim: When Zedekiah's appeal to Egypt briefly draws the Chaldeans away, Jeremiah predicts that Pharaoh's troops will return home and Babylon will return to burn Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: هوذا الآن جند فرعون يرجعون إلى أرض مصر , ويرجع الكلدانيون ويقاتلون هذه القرية ويحتوون عليها ويحرقونها بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews accused Jeremiah of defecting and imprisoned him; Zedekiah privately asked his prophecy, but feared his nobles and returned him to custody.
rows.anchor: ثم إن اليهود اتهموا إرميا بأنه يريد أن يفر إلى الكلدانيين فجلدوه وطرحوه في السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The princes sought to kill Jeremiah because his advice to surrender would discourage Jerusalem's defenders, but Zedekiah admitted he could not override his nobles.
rows.anchor: يقتل هذا الرجل لأنه يسقط أيادي المقاتلة الذين بقوا في القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The princes threw Jeremiah into a muddy cistern, but the believing Ethiopian Ebed-Melech rescued him; God promised to spare Ebed-Melech because he trusted God's word.
rows.anchor: وسمع عبد الملك حبشي وكان رجلا مؤمنا فقال للملك : يا سيدي ! بئس ما صنع هؤلاء القوم بالنبي

rows.speaker: إرميا
rows.claim: Jeremiah again urges Zedekiah to surrender to Babylon to save his life; the king fears that the Judeans will mock him, but Jeremiah assures him they will not hand him over.
rows.anchor: هكذا يقول الرب إله إسرائيل : لئن خرجت إلى أشراف ملك بابل لتحيين نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Babylon captured Jerusalem in Zedekiah's ninth year and destroyed it in his eleventh; the king fled, was captured near Jericho, saw his sons killed, and was blinded and taken to Babylon.
rows.anchor: وفي إحدى عشرة سنة لصديقيا في الشهر الخامس انثملت القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Babylonians burned the palace and houses, demolished Jerusalem's wall, deported most survivors, and left the poorest people under Gedaliah's rule.
rows.anchor: وأحرق بيت الملك وبيوت الشعب بالنار , واستأصل السور المحيط بأورشليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nebuzaradan freed Jeremiah and acknowledged that God had brought disaster on Jerusalem because its people sinned and did not heed him; this history illustrates the attackers' great force.
rows.anchor: إلهك الذي قال هذا الشر على هذه البلدة وفعل كالذي قال , لأنكم أخطأتم للرب ولم تسمعوا صوته

rows.speaker: يوسف بن كريون
rows.claim: Josephus ben Gorion's history says Rome sought peace and security from Nebuchadnezzar after he took Jerusalem, ending the Chaldean-Roman wars until Darius.
rows.anchor: أن الروم لما بلغهم أن بختنصر ملك بابل فتح مدينة المقدس ازداد خوفهم من الكسدانيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says the Chaldeans fought Rome after Rome aided the Greeks, then God raised Darius of Media and Cyrus of Persia to end Chaldean rule.
rows.anchor: أثار من ملوك الأمم ملكين عظيمين : أحدهما دارا ملك ماداي , والآخر كورش ملك الفرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belshazzar desecrated the Jerusalem Temple's sacred gold and silver vessels by using them for wine at a feast and praising idols; God was angered by this sacrilege and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: فسخط الله سبحانه من ذلك وكره مكا فعله بلتشصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An angel wrote a warning on the wall before Belshazzar; Daniel interpreted «numbered, weighed, divided»: the kingdom's time had ended, the king was found wanting, and rule would pass to Cyrus and Darius.
rows.anchor: فأما هذه الألفاظ المكتوبة فهي ( حسب ووزن ونقل ) وتفسيرها أن الله حسب مدة دولتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belshazzar was murdered that night; Cyrus and Darius learned of the desecration and prophecy, praised God, and Cyrus vowed to rebuild the Temple, return its vessels, and release the Jewish exiles.
rows.anchor: ونذر كورش أنه يبني بيت الله بأورشليم , ويرد تلك الآنية , ويطلق جالية اليهود أن يرجعوا إلى بلادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cyrus and Darius conquered Babylon and divided the Chaldean realm, with Darius taking Babylon and Cyrus taking the other territories.
rows.anchor: ثم اقتسم دارا وكورش مملكة الكسدانيين فأخذ دارا مدينة بابل وأعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cyrus invited Jewish exiles to return and provided the money and materials needed to rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: وأنا كورش عبد الإله العظيم أطلق من خزائني جميع ما يحتاج إليه من المال والعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cyrus supplied yearly money, grain, oil, wine, livestock, and other resources for Temple worship; the Persian kings continued this support after him.
rows.anchor: وكان كورش يطلق لهم كل سنة ما يحتاجون إليه لخدمة بيت الله من المال والحنطة والزيت والخمر والغنم والبقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted Cyrus victories and treasure in recompense for helping Israel, as Isaiah had prophesied.
rows.anchor: كما أخبر الله تعالى على يد أشيعا النبي عليه السلام أنه يفعل ذلك بكورش من أجل إحسانه إلى بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: أشيعا بن آموص
rows.claim: Isaiah's prophecy says Cyrus will carry out God's will, rebuild Jerusalem and its Temple, and subdue nations through God's aid; God says he called Cyrus before Cyrus knew him.
rows.anchor: قال في سفر الأنبياء في نبوة أشيعا بن آموص : هكذا يقول الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian kings continued honoring the Temple until Ahasuerus and Haman turned circumstances against the Jews; a Jewish wife then moved the king to favor them, and their fortunes continued under Persia until Alexander.
rows.anchor: حتى كان أحشويرش - وهو أردشير الملك - فتغيرت حال اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author traces later Jewish rule through Alexander, the Greeks, and Rome, then says widespread corruption and violence led to their second destruction under Titus; their political order never recovered.
rows.anchor: ثم سلط عليهم طيطوس قيصر فأهلكهم وأخرب البيت الخراب الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author names the killing of Zechariah and John and the attempt to kill Jesus as grave offenses preceding the second punishment.
rows.anchor: وقتلوا زكريا ويحيى وابنه عليهما السلام , وأطبقوا على إرادة قتل المسيح ابن مريم عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good conduct benefits the doer: obedience to the Book's call to justice and excellence brings God's support and honor in this life, the next, or both.
rows.anchor: بفعل الطاعة على حسب الأمر في الكتاب الداعي إلى العدل والإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoing harms its perpetrators; the feminine pronoun in «فلها» rhetorically distances the ugliness of evil from the self and increases aversion to it.
rows.anchor: { وإن أسأتم } أي بارتكاب المحرمات والإفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second punishment follows Israel's restored victory, marking the short interval before renewed judgment and their liability for corruption, especially killing Zechariah and John and plotting against Jesus.
rows.anchor: فاستأهلتم البلاء لما أفسدتم وأحدثتم من البلايا التي أعظمها قتل زكريا ويحيى عليهما السلام والعزم على قتل عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning also threatens Quraysh: their security in Mecca could turn to fear and humiliation if they did not repent, although the conquest of Mecca came as an honor through Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعريض بالتهديد لقريش بأنهم إن لم يرجعوا أبدل أمنهم في الحرم خوفا وعزمهم ذلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hostile attackers would enter the Jerusalem mosque as enemies had before, defeat Israel's forces, and destroy what they had conquered.
rows.anchor: كما دخلوه } أي الأعداء { أول مرة } بالسيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «ليتبروا» means to ruin and destroy with cutting apart.
rows.anchor: أي يهلكوا ويدمروا مع التقطيع والتفريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming punishment arrives as a compelled event, contrary to the wishes of those it reaches.
rows.anchor: أي أتى إتيانا هو كالملجأ إليه قسرا على خلاف ما يريده الآتي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quotes the Torah's covenant curses as a prediction of the second calamity: depopulation, dispersion among nations, exile, fear, and eventual return to Egypt.
rows.anchor: وقال في التوراة إشارة إلى هذه المرة الأخيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Torah passage repeats the same curses quoted for the first calamity, the author takes this passage to indicate the second occasion; he says learned Jews reported that their scholars agree.
rows.anchor: وإنما قلت : إن هذا إشارة إلى المرة الثانية , لأنه تكرير لذلك الذي قدمته في الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second destruction occurred under Titus after his father Vespasian became ruler of Rome; Josephus ben Gorion, captured during the revolt, accompanied Titus.
rows.anchor: وكان الخراب في هذه المرة على يد طيطوس بعد أن تملك أبوه أسفسيانوس على الروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Ezra's reconstruction the Temple stood for 420 years; after Titus destroyed it the Jews never regained control, and the destruction came 380 years into Alexander's rule.
rows.anchor: بعد أن استمر البيت عامرا م عمارة العزير عليه السلام أربعمائة سنة وعشرين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parses «ما» as a verbal noun, meaning the duration of Israel's ascendancy; this makes «يتبروا» intransitive and broadens its sense.
rows.anchor: ما مصدرية , أي مدة علوهم فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic infinitive «تتبيرا» intensifies the verb and confirms the certainty of the promised destruction.
rows.anchor: وأكد الفعل وحقق الوعد فقال : { تتبيرا * }
